DE-C1-01-001.notes: gedenken (commemorate) takes a genitive object: der Opfer (genitive plural). It's used in speeches and on memorials; the noun is das Gedenken.

DE-C1-01-002.notes: bedürfen (require) takes the genitive: keiner Erklärung. In everyday German, brauchen + accusative is used instead.

DE-C1-01-003.notes: sich bedienen (make use of) takes the genitive: eines Tricks. sich bedienen without an object means 'help oneself'.

DE-C1-01-004.notes: sich der Stimme enthalten = abstain from voting. The genitive object is fixed in this phrase; the noun is die Enthaltung.

DE-C1-01-005.notes: sich (dative) einer Sache bewusst sein takes the genitive: des Risikos. Risiko is neuter, so the genitive adds -s.

DE-C1-01-006.notes: anklagen + genitive of the charge: des Diebstahls angeklagt. Modern legal German also uses wegen + genitive.

DE-C1-01-007.notes: würdig (worthy) takes the genitive: einer Antwort würdig. The adjective follows its object, as with bewusst.

DE-C1-02-001.notes: es sei denn (unless) is a frozen Konjunktiv I. It's followed by main-clause word order (es regnet) or a dass-clause.

DE-C1-02-002.notes: Sei es … oder … means 'whether … or…'. The Konjunktiv I sei opens the phrase, which stands apart from the main clause.

DE-C1-02-003.notes: Wie dem auch sei = be that as it may. It closes a digression and returns to the main point. dem here is the old dative of das, referring to the situation.

DE-C1-02-004.notes: Recipes traditionally use man + Konjunktiv I as an instruction: Man nehme… Modern recipes use the imperative or infinitive.

DE-C1-02-005.notes: Es lebe …! (Long live…!) is a Konjunktiv I wish. The noun that follows is the subject: die Freiheit.

DE-C1-02-006.notes: koste es, was es wolle = whatever it costs. Both koste and wolle are Konjunktiv I. It's set off by commas from the main clause.

DE-C1-03-001.notes: A participle phrase can replace a time clause: In Berlin angekommen = als er in Berlin angekommen war. It's written style.

DE-C1-03-002.notes: ehrlich gesagt (to be honest) is a fixed participle phrase. It counts as position one, so the verb habe comes next.

DE-C1-03-003.notes: genau genommen = strictly speaking. Likewise streng genommen, kurz gesagt. The participle phrase takes first position, so hast follows.

DE-C1-03-004.notes: abgesehen davon = apart from that. davon can be replaced by von + dative: abgesehen von dem Preis. It's usually followed by a comma when it comes first.

DE-C1-03-005.notes: vorausgesetzt, (dass) = provided (that). The weather mitspielen means 'play along, cooperate'. With dass dropped, a main clause follows: vorausgesetzt, das Wetter spielt mit.

DE-C1-03-006.notes: Gesetzt den Fall, (dass) … = supposing (that). The accusative den Fall is frozen in the phrase. angenommen, (dass) is a more neutral synonym.

DE-C1-04-001.notes: im Rahmen + genitive = as part of, within the framework of. It's frequent in business and official reports.

DE-C1-04-002.notes: seitens + genitive = on the part of. In speech, von is used instead. It's typical of reports: seitens der Regierung.

DE-C1-04-003.notes: zwecks + genitive = for the purpose of. With a noun without article, the genitive doesn't show: zwecks Terminvereinbarung.

DE-C1-04-004.notes: mangels + genitive = for lack of. With a plural noun and no article, the dative appears instead: mangels Beweisen.

DE-C1-04-005.notes: zuzüglich (plus) and abzüglich (minus) take the genitive and are common on invoices. Mehrwertsteuer (VAT) is often abbreviated MwSt.

DE-C1-04-006.notes: unter Berücksichtigung + genitive = taking into account. The phrase takes first position, so haben comes next.

DE-C1-04-007.notes: im Zuge + genitive = in the course of, as part of a process. It's typical of news reports. Zuge is the dative of Zug with the old -e.

DE-C1-05-001.notes: ver- can mean doing something wrongly: verschlafen = oversleep. Inseparable, so no ge-: verschlafen.

DE-C1-05-002.notes: sich verlaufen = get lost on foot; sich verfahren = by car. Both use ver- in the sense 'wrongly'. sich verlaufen also means 'disperse' of crowds.

DE-C1-05-003.notes: zer- means 'to pieces': zerbrechen, zerreißen, zerstören. zerbrechen without an object takes sein. With an object it takes haben: Er hat das Glas zerbrochen.

DE-C1-05-004.notes: er- often means achieving something by effort: erarbeiten (earn through work), erkämpfen (win by fighting).

DE-C1-05-005.notes: ent- means 'away from, escape': entkommen + dative (escape someone). It takes sein. The dative der Polizei is the thing escaped from.

DE-C1-05-006.notes: antworten takes auf + accusative; beantworten takes a direct accusative object. be- turns the prepositional verb into a transitive one.

DE-C1-06-001.notes: -erweise turns an adjective into a sentence adverb that comments on the whole: glücklicherweise (fortunately).

DE-C1-06-002.notes: möglicherweise = possibly, perhaps. It's more formal than vielleicht. It can stand anywhere in the middle field.

DE-C1-06-003.notes: -weise added to a noun means 'in a … way': teilweise (partly). There's no -er- with nouns. It can also be an adjective: eine teilweise Sperrung.

DE-C1-06-004.notes: schrittweise = step by step. Before a noun it can be used as an adjective: eine schrittweise Einführung.

DE-C1-06-005.notes: beispielsweise = for example; it's more formal than zum Beispiel and is set off by commas. It's often abbreviated z. B. in its synonym zum Beispiel.

DE-C1-07-001.notes: Leaving out wenn puts the verb first: Hätte ich das gewusst = wenn ich das gewusst hätte. The main clause often starts with dann or so.

DE-C1-07-002.notes: Sollten Sie … = should you … is a formal conditional with the verb first. It's common in business letters.

DE-C1-07-003.notes: Kaum hatte er …, als … = no sooner had he … than. Kaum takes first position, so hatte follows. The als-clause has its verb at the end.

DE-C1-07-004.notes: The second part of kaum … als is introduced by als, with the verb at the end of the als-clause. The als here is not comparative but temporal.
DE-C1-07-004.text: Kaum war sie zu Hause, {{c1::als::than (kaum … , …)}} es zu regnen begann.
DE-C1-07-004.tr: She'd barely got home when it started to rain.
DE-C1-07-004.flag: dup: replaced Kaum hatte er sich hingesetzt, als das Telefon klingelte (same sentence as C1-07-003)

DE-C1-07-005.notes: Wäre das Wetter besser = wenn das Wetter besser wäre. The verb-first form is neutral in speech too. The main clause starts with its own verb: könnten wir.

DE-C1-08-001.notes: zumal (especially as) adds a strengthening reason and sends the verb to the end. It's more formal than weil.
DE-C1-08-001.text: Wir nehmen ein Taxi, {{c1::zumal::especially as}} es schon spät ist.
DE-C1-08-001.tr: We'll take a taxi, especially as it's already late.
DE-C1-08-001.flag: dup: replaced Ich bleibe zu Hause, zumal ich erkältet bin (near-identical to A2-01-002)

DE-C1-08-002.notes: wohingegen (whereas) contrasts two parallel facts and sends the verb to the end. während can be used in the same sense.

DE-C1-08-003.notes: geschweige denn (let alone) follows a negative or near-negative statement: kaum laufen, geschweige denn rennen.

DE-C1-08-004.notes: insofern …, als = in so far as. insofern goes in the main clause, als starts the subordinate clause.

DE-C1-08-005.notes: obgleich (although) is a formal synonym of obwohl; wenngleich is another. The main clause starts with the verb arbeitete.

DE-C1-08-006.notes: nichtsdestotrotz (nevertheless) is an adverb, so the verb follows it. It's slightly humorous in speech.

DE-C1-08-007.notes: folglich (consequently) is an adverb: the verb follows. demzufolge and somit are synonyms. It can also stand inside the clause: wurde folglich abgelehnt.

DE-C1-08-008.notes: wo … doch means 'when, even though' and expresses indignation: Er schweigt, wo er doch alles weiß. doch in the clause is essential to the meaning.

DE-C1-08-009.notes: Nicht dass + Konjunktiv II means 'not that…': Nicht dass ich etwas dagegen hätte. The clause is incomplete, ending in aber…

DE-C1-08-010.notes: ehe (before) is a literary synonym of bevor, with the verb at the end. It's common in older literature and fixed phrases such as ehe man sich's versieht.

DE-C1-08-011.notes: sowie as a conjunction means 'as soon as', like sobald. As a connector it means 'as well as'. It's typical of formal and written German.

DE-C1-09-001.notes: davon ausgehen, dass … = assume that. The prepositional verb ausgehen von needs the da-word davon before a dass-clause.

DE-C1-09-002.notes: dafür sorgen, dass … = make sure that. sorgen für + accusative becomes dafür. The imperative Sorgen Sie is formal.

DE-C1-09-003.notes: Das liegt daran, dass … = that's because… liegen an + dative becomes daran. woran liegt das? asks for the cause.

DE-C1-09-004.notes: darauf hinweisen, dass … = point out that. hinweisen auf + accusative becomes darauf; the prefix hin goes to the end.

DE-C1-09-005.notes: sich darauf verlassen, dass … = count on (something happening). verlassen auf + accusative becomes darauf.

DE-C1-10-001.notes: bekommen + participle forms a passive with the recipient as subject: Ich bekomme das Paket geschickt. kriegen is the colloquial version.

DE-C1-10-002.notes: Perfekt of the bekommen-passive: hat … geschenkt bekommen. The giver can be added with von. bekommen here is the participle; it has no ge-.

DE-C1-10-003.notes: Es wird gebeten, … is an impersonal passive used in notices: you are requested to… It avoids naming anyone.

DE-C1-10-004.notes: The past passive in Konjunktiv II with a modal: hätte gemacht werden müssen. The modal infinitive goes last.

DE-C1-10-005.notes: wäre … worden is the past passive Konjunktiv II: wäre gebaut worden (would have been built). The wenn-clause also uses Konjunktiv II: gegeben hätte.

DE-C1-11-001.notes: der See (masculine) is a lake: im See. die See (feminine) is the sea, mostly in fixed phrases. The plural of der See is die Seen.
DE-C1-11-001.tip: der See = lake; die See = sea.

DE-C1-11-002.notes: die See (sea) appears in auf See (at sea), an die See. Otherwise das Meer is used. die See has no plural in this sense.

DE-C1-11-003.notes: die Steuer (tax) has the plural Steuern. das Steuer (steering wheel) is rarely plural. The verb zahlen takes a direct object: Steuern zahlen.

DE-C1-11-004.notes: das Steuer (steering wheel): am Steuer sitzen = be at the wheel. The neuter gives am (an dem). The verb is steuern (steer).

DE-C1-11-005.notes: Bank meaning 'bench' has the plural Bänke, with an umlaut. The dative plural is den Bänken. The two meanings share one singular, die Bank.

DE-C1-11-006.notes: Bank meaning a financial institution has the plural Banken. Both meanings are feminine in the singular.

DE-C1-11-007.notes: Wörter is the plural for separate words, as in a dictionary or a count. Wörterbuch itself is built on Wörter.

DE-C1-11-008.notes: Worte is the plural for words said, a statement or speech: freundliche Worte. In set phrases: mit anderen Worten (in other words).
DE-C1-11-008.tip: Wörter (separate words) vs Worte (what someone said).

DE-C1-11-009.notes: der Leiter (manager, head) vs die Leiter (ladder). The article is the only marker of meaning. die Leiter has the plural die Leitern.

DE-C1-11-010.notes: der Kiefer (jaw) vs die Kiefer (pine tree). Mir tut … weh uses the dative experiencer. die Kiefer has the plural die Kiefern.

DE-C1-11-011.notes: der Erbe (heir, an n-noun) vs das Erbe (inheritance). der Erbe takes -n in all other cases: den Erben.

DE-C1-11-012.notes: das Gehalt (salary, plural Gehälter) vs der Gehalt (content, proportion). Gehalt an + dative gives the content of something.

DE-C1-12-001.notes: als + Konjunktiv II verb straight after it means 'as if': als wäre nichts geschehen. It's the same as als ob … wäre.

DE-C1-12-002.notes: als hätte sie … = as if she had… The verb comes straight after als, and the participle goes to the end.

DE-C1-12-003.notes: als ob keeps verb-final order: als ob jemand weint. In speech the indicative is common after als ob; writing prefers Konjunktiv II.

DE-C1-13-001.notes: stolz auf + accusative = proud of: stolz auf dich. The noun is der Stolz. With a clause, the da-word appears: stolz darauf, dass…

DE-C1-13-002.notes: gespannt auf + accusative = eager to know, curious about. It suggests suspense. Ich bin gespannt, ob… is common too.

DE-C1-13-003.notes: abhängig von + dative = dependent on, as with the verb abhängen von. The noun is die Abhängigkeit von.

DE-C1-13-004.notes: zufrieden mit + dative = satisfied with. The noun is die Zufriedenheit. The opposite is unzufrieden mit.

DE-C1-13-005.notes: verantwortlich für + accusative = responsible for. The noun is die Verantwortung für. With a clause: verantwortlich dafür, dass…

DE-C1-13-006.notes: interessiert an + dative = interested in, unlike the verb sich interessieren für + accusative. With a clause: interessiert daran, dass…
DE-C1-13-006.tip: interessiert an (adjective) vs sich interessieren für (verb).

DE-C1-14-001.notes: Unstressed pronouns move ahead of a noun subject in the middle of the clause: hat ihn mein Bruder angerufen.

DE-C1-14-002.notes: Two pronoun objects go ahead of the noun subject, accusative first: hat es uns der Kellner gebracht.
DE-C1-14-002.text: Später hat {{c1::es::it · accusative (before a noun subject)}} uns der Kellner gebracht.
DE-C1-14-002.tr: Later the waiter brought it to us.
DE-C1-14-002.flag: dup: replaced Dann hat es ihr der Lehrer erklärt (near-identical to A2-07-009 Der Lehrer hat es gut erklärt)

DE-C1-14-003.notes: dessen as a possessive removes ambiguity: Paul und dessen Frau means Paul's wife; seine could be Peter's.

DE-C1-14-004.notes: derer is the genitive plural pointing forward to a relative clause: die Zahl derer, die zustimmen. The singular equivalents are dessen and deren.

DE-C1-14-005.notes: manch can stand uninflected before einer: manch einer (many a person). It's literary. With a noun: manch ein Mensch, or inflected mancher Mensch.

DE-C1-14-006.notes: solch can stand uninflected before ein: solch ein Unsinn. In speech, so ein is far more common. Inflected, it becomes solcher: solcher Unsinn.
